newsitem.title: UK: Spice Girls hail "girl power" in UK parliament.
newsitem.headline: Spice Girls hail "girl power" in UK parliament.

text.p: British pop quintet the Spice Girls, musical crusaders for "girl power", said on Sunday they were delighted at the record number of women elected to Britain's parliament on May 1.
"It's great that girls are successful, in the music industry or any industry," Melanie Chisholm, known as "Sporty Spice" told reporters at a news conference to promote a sponsorship deal.

"I'm very pleased about that, very pleased," added "Ginger Spice" Geri Halliwell. But she said she doubted the Spice Girls had anything to do with the election of more than 100 women to parliament on May 1.
"It's just a reflection of the 1990s," she said.

The Spice Girls have claimed former Conservative prime minister Margaret Thatcher as their heroine and "the first ever Spice Girl". But they avoided passing any judgment on the Labour Party's crushing election victory.
The five women have topped the charts in 31 countries and even outdid the Beatles by getting their first single "Wannabe" to number one in the United States.
